summary.one_liner: Zabbix is an open-source, enterprise-class distributed monitoring solution for tracking the performance and availability of network devices, servers, services, and other IT resources.
summary.what_it_does: Zabbix discovers network entities and server resources and supports onboarding and offboarding of devices, using templates for out-of-the-box integrations. It acquires metrics with agent or agent-less approaches from sources such as devices, operating systems, virtualization and container platforms (Docker, Kubernetes), cloud infrastructure, databases, webpages, Java application servers, and API endpoints. It performs real-time problem detection, correlates problems, and attempts root cause analysis. It sends alerts through channels including Slack, JIRA, Microsoft Teams, email, and text messages. Collected data and events can be visualized as graphs, lists, geomaps, and network topology maps, and the README also mentions multitenancy, distributed monitoring of remote locations behind firewalls, reporting, auditing, and service SLA calculations.
use_cases: monitor server and network device performance
get alerts when IT services go down
build dashboards and network topology maps
track service SLAs across multiple data centers
how_to_run: Follow the installation manual (linked in README)
notable: Agent and agent-less metric acquisition from many source types
Distributed monitoring with remote command execution behind firewalls
Root cause analysis and problem correlation
Streams metrics and events over HTTP
caveats: README gives no installation commands; setup is described only by linking to the installation manual
Enterprise-scale feature set may be heavier than needed for simple single-host monitoring
